headline: Sagar-Runi murder: Evidence points to cultural personality's involvement
summary: The ICT chief prosecutor reveals a new lead in the 14-year-old murder case of journalist couple Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.
details: Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), Md Aminul Islam, stated that investigators have found preliminary evidence suggesting a cultural personality was involved in the murder of Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.
The prosecutor declined to reveal the identity of the individual, citing the need to protect the ongoing investigation.
This new lead emerged while investigators were probing a separate case, according to a prosecutor's statement on Thursday.
Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were killed at their flat in Dhaka's Poshchim Rajabazar on February 11, 2012.
While the prosecution team has made these claims, an official from the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) told The Daily Star that they have not received such information yet.
The PBI official added that they would consult with the prosecution team to clarify the matter.
caption:
A new lead after 14 years: Evidence suggests a cultural personality was involved in the murder of journalists Sagar and Runi.

Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT), Md Aminul Islam, stated that investigators have found preliminary evidence suggesting a cultural personality was involved in the murder of Sagar Sarowar and Meherun Runi.

The prosecutor declined to reveal the identity of the individual, citing the need to protect the ongoing investigation.

This new lead emerged while investigators were probing a separate case, according to a prosecutor's statement on Thursday.

Sagar Sarowar, news editor of Maasranga Television, and Meherun Runi, a senior reporter at ATN Bangla, were killed at their flat in Dhaka's Poshchim Rajabazar on February 11, 2012.

While the prosecution team has made these claims, an official from the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) told The Daily Star that they have not received such information yet.

The PBI official added that they would consult with the prosecution team to clarify the matter.

headline_marked: Tk 902cr needed to [[operationalize HSIA third terminal]], says Minister
headline: Tk 902cr needed to operationalize HSIA third terminal, says Minister
summary: Civil Aviation Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat stated that the previous government inaugurated the building without completing essential internal works.
details: Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat told Parliament on Sunday that the newly built third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) requires Tk 902 crore to become fully operational.
The Minister revealed that the previous government inaugurated the building as if it were complete, but critical internal works remain unfinished.
The government is now working to complete these tasks, with approximately 57% of Operational Readiness and Airport Transfer (ORAT) work already finished.
Minister Millat emphasized that leaving a $2.1 billion asset idle would be a loss for the state and that operationalizing it would help in repaying JICA loans more quickly.
Once the third terminal is open, the airport's passenger capacity will double, which is expected to increase revenue and facilitate loan repayments.
The Minister also mentioned that the government is reviewing contracts for nine new aircraft purchased during the previous administration to check for irregularities.
caption:
Tk 902 crore is required to finally open the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat told Parliament on Sunday that the newly built third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport (HSIA) requires Tk 902 crore to become fully operational.

The Minister revealed that the previous government inaugurated the building as if it were complete, but critical internal works remain unfinished.

The government is now working to complete these tasks, with approximately 57% of Operational Readiness and Airport Transfer (ORAT) work already finished.

Minister Millat emphasized that leaving a $2.1 billion asset idle would be a loss for the state and that operationalizing it would help in repaying JICA loans more quickly.

Once the third terminal is open, the airport's passenger capacity will double, which is expected to increase revenue and facilitate loan repayments.

The Minister also mentioned that the government is reviewing contracts for nine new aircraft purchased during the previous administration to check for irregularities.
